themes.name: AI-Enhanced Critical Thinking Development
themes.definition: Integration of AI tools and frameworks to systematically promote critical thinking skills through structured interventions and reflective practices. This includes explicit mentions of enhanced analytical reasoning, problem-solving, and evaluative thinking outcomes.
evidence: [Chen2024a] 'PP-iGAI approach could better promote students' learning achievement [...] critical thinking'
[Yuriev2025] 'GenAI can be a powerful tool for [...] critical thinking when paired with structured guidance'

themes.name: Interactive AI Agents for Skill Development
themes.definition: Use of AI chatbots, agents, or co-actors that simulate social interactions to develop domain-specific and transferable skills through scenario-based learning experiences.
evidence: [Littell2025] 'AI-powered chatbots enrich student learning and foster critical thinking by providing authentic experiences'
[Bayly-Castaneda2025] 'AI agents produced enhanced critical thinking through scenario-based simulations'
[Katsenou2025] 'critical inquiry and analytical reasoning [...] through structured dialog with AI'

themes.name: Structured Prompt Engineering and Scaffolding
themes.definition: Implementation of deliberate pedagogical strategies involving progressive prompts, scaffolded feedback, and prompt engineering to guide cognitive development and technology-mediated learning.
evidence: [Chen2024a] 'progressive prompts-based image-GAI [...] progressively provide students with clues and guidance'
[Nathaniel2025] 'prompt specificity and scaffolded feedback improved engagement'

themes.name: Ethical and Cognitive Challenges of AI Integration
themes.definition: Identified limitations and concerns regarding AI implementation in education, including ethical dilemmas, cognitive risks, and technological limitations requiring mitigation strategies.
evidence: [Bora2025] 'risks of superficial application' and 'exposure to misinformation'
[Sudo2025] 'algorithm aversion' affecting perception of AI-generated feedback

themes.name: AI-Assisted Cognitive Engagement Strategies
themes.definition: Development of techniques to maintain and enhance cognitive engagement through AI-mediated tools, including metacognitive support, personalized learning trajectories, and attention management interventions.
evidence: [Teng2026] 'GenAI playfulness and perceived learning value [...] enhance students' cognitive engagement'
[Zhai2025] 'AI applications facilitate independent academic exploration and enhance learners’ motivation'
[Liu2026] 'GAICW scaffolds complex thinking processes, particularly in early design phases'

data.meta_observations: Recurring emphasis on critical thinking as both outcome and process, frequent integration of structured prompting techniques, and ethical concerns transcending multiple domains. Notable absence of explicit mention of AI literacy frameworks despite extensive focus on cognitive skills development. Methodological diversity challenges direct comparisons between pedagogical approaches.
data.grounding_notes: All themes directly supported by cited quotes from listed articles. Some concepts like 'deepfake detection' (Weigelt2026) and 'distributed creativity' (Perdana2026) appeared insufficiently connected to main themes for inclusion despite relevance. Ethical considerations consistently present but rarely dominant in abstract-level discourse.
